headline: Strategy Shifts to Daily Payments to Jumpstart Funding Machine
author: David Pan

paragraphs.text: (Bloomberg) -- Strategy Inc.'s flagship preferred shares will soon begin paying a daily dividend, the latest maneuver by Michael Saylor to revive the Bitcoin accumulator's sputtering fundraising machine.

Shareholders approved the change Wednesday, the second attempt in less than five months to jumpstart demand for what Saylor — the co-founder and chairman — has designated as the company's main funding source. In June, Strategy shifted to semi-monthly payments from monthly while the price of the STRC preferred issue tumbled along with the value of the cryptocurrency.

Saylor is counting on the daily payments to be enough of an incentive to restart demand from individual investors, who were among the biggest buyers of the securities when they were first introduced last year. Strategy needs the securities — which offer a 12% annual yield — to trade at par or higher to make them economical to issue. Daily payments are scheduled to begin Nov. 1.

In a statement Thursday, Strategy reiterated that it returned to profitability in the third quarter after registering a $21 billion unrealized gain from the increase in the value of its holdings during crypto's late summer rally. Net income was $19.5 billion.

The road back hasn't been easy. Last week, the biggest corporate holder of Bitcoin increased the size of its STRC buyback by 50% to $3 billion. In the meantime, it has continued to sell common stock to buy Bitcoin, diluting existing shareholders.

While the common stock rallied around 75% in the third quarter, it remains roughly 70% below the historic all-time high established during the post-election euphoria of November 2024. The stock was little changed in after-hours trading.

"The improved financing position came at a cost," Managing Director Brian Dobson and Equity Research Director Greg Pendy at the investment bank Clear Street, wrote in a recent report. "The repurchases lowered the preferred dividend burden, but came at a cost to common shareholders, as share issuance outpaced Bitcoin accumulation during the quarter."

Strategy has been seeking to tap the enduring appetite for income, especially among retail investors. For companies accumulating Bitcoin, which generates no income of its own, that demand offers a way to keep raising capital despite growing strains on the model pioneered by Saylor.

That retail demand hasn't been missed by others, with some competitors even paying dividends higher than the 12% offered on STRC. Strive Inc. sold $630 million in preferred shares with a 15% annual dividend last week. That's more than triple what you earn on a top-rated one-year US Treasury note, and comparable to distressed debt returns.

Returning to the $1 billion or more weekly Bitcoin purchases by Strategy that captured the attention of the crypto market in the first half of the year may not happen soon, according to Pendy and Dobson.
"We assume no new preferred issuance in the fourth quarter and $1.59 billion per quarter in 2027," Clear Street wrote. "The pace and cost of issuance remain important to our outlook."
